resolved_conflicts.field: Grande Prairie Museum tower: origin and history
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Downstream News Media says the tower was built in the 1930s, came from the Smoky River area and was in use until the 1970s. TheRegional quotes Alberta Wildfire saying it was a training tower, never really a forestry tower, and that it was moved by helicopter in the 70s or early 80s. The story keeps this tower out of the Smoky site's history and only warns readers not to confuse the two, because neither source ties it to this site.

notes_for_editor: PROTECTED DATA, decide before publishing: the brief's build year (2013), height, elevation, access and status come from the Alberta Wildfire WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT layer (cached in data/raw/expansion/prairies-north/ab_wf_wildfire_lookout_attrs.json and data/raw/web/). Its metadata (data/raw/expansion/prairies-north/ab_lookout_layer0_meta.json) classifies the layer as Protected and says its features are not to be displayed on maps the general public will see at scales larger than 1:1,000,000. None of those values is in the story or facts. NO PUBLIC SOURCE found for this site's build, staffing, fate or access. The Grande Prairie Museum tower is a different structure and the sources disagree on its history (see resolved_conflicts); if it is ever linked to this record, it needs a source that names the Smoky site. The 2024 count of eight towers covers the whole Grande Prairie Forest Area, not this site. Confidence low; consider holding the story until an official source turns up.
